description: We are a team from Cerro Azul in NASA Space Apps 2026. Our goal is building a real-time app to predict and monitor flood risks using NASA Earth observation & SAR satellite data. We have experience in Python, software development, and data analysis. Looking for teammates with skills in GIS/satellite imagery, UI/UX frontend design, AI/ML models, or presentation and storytelling.
summary: We developed SPILL NASA, a real-time flood monitoring and early prediction mobile application specifically engineered to protect communities in the Álamo Temapache region of Veracruz, Mexico. Our system integrates Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data processing from the Sentinel-1 satellite alongside key hydrometeorological variables, including accumulated precipitation, maximum humidity, and water volume. By leveraging SAR microwave imaging, SPILL NASA penetrates dense cloud cover and operates continuously day and night during severe storms, accurately mapping water extent and soil saturation when traditional optical sensors are blinded. Through an intuitive interface featuring a dynamic predictive system, historical radar queries, and a standardized early warning traffic-light system (Normal, Precaution, Alert, and Danger/Evacuation), the tool translates complex geospatial data into accessible, actionable intelligence for both citizens and Civil Protection authorities. This approach democratizes orbital-grade Earth observation, reducing response times to local basin overflows and strengthening community resilience against hydrometeorological disasters.
details:
"SPILL NASA" has the function of predicting floods by implementing an algorithm that takes into account the use of Precipitation Indices and Humidity Indices, using open data from NASA.

The app auto-adjusts the parameters of the algorithm for each zone, thanks to the implementation of the SAR radar which is a satellite that collects data from radio frequency waves, delivering results to verify that the prediction was accurate in the delimited location (North Zone of Veracruz, Mexico).

The humidity and precipitation rates that our app collects allow the system to monitor, calculate with an approximate advance of 3 days and alert the population about the imminent risk of a possible flood.

During the flood of October 11, 2025 in the northern area of Veracruz it seemed to have no indications; when collecting data, humidity rates plus precipitation rates showed an increase in both rates just before a flood was not a simple coincidence, if people had known this data would have been acted on in advance.

Safeguarding people’s lives by using data that is already accessible to all and displaying it in a user-friendly, user-accessible system is the impact we seek.

It was used during the development of Android Studio encoded in Java, using IMEG’s AIR humidity, WorldView NASA and SAR Sentinel-1 systems for precipitation.

Algorithms, indexes, satellites, are things that are not shown in the app, it is about showing an intuitive and understandable interface for our target audience young and adults. Our app combines key satellite information for greater certainty in data collection.

In addition, "SPILL NASA" has a traffic light that allows the population to identify risk levels in their area.

The moisture rates in soil absorption were taken into account, to know whether a soil behaved as a sponge or as a swimming pool against precipitation, height and topography of the area, data taken by the satellite Sentinel-1. In the future, it is expected to implement a dedicated server to compare expected results with SAR system data on water volumes.
